headline: A 10-member permissioned oDAO can repoint any network contract in RocketStorage (T1) after a 7-day on-chain vote delay plus an upgrade delay whose value could not be re-read on-chain; pDAO parameter/treasury path is a much slower 21-day RPL-weighted vote.
short_headline: oDAO holds T1 upgrade behind 7d+ delay

findings.text: RocketStorage 0x1d8f8f00cfa6758d7bE78336684788Fb0ee0Fa46 is the root address registry. getDeployedStatus() returns true and getGuardian() returns 0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e at block 25883993. There is no owner()/admin()/governor() on the registry; authority is expressed by which contract names are registered in storage.

Both bootstrap authorities are retired: RocketDAONodeTrusted 0xb8e783882b11Ff4f6Cef3C501EA0f4b960152cc9 getBootstrapModeDisabled() = true (block 25778186) and RocketDAOProtocol 0x0429Cdd8cEACe24d4dC2B97Ce22A780a407dF0e1 getBootstrapModeDisabled() = true (block 25793758). The guardian's bootstrapUpgrade / bootstrapSetting* / bootstrapSpendTreasury entrypoints on those two contracts are therefore not usable, so the guardian EOA is not a live T1 path.

No proxy pattern is in use on the contracts inspected. /api/contract/abi for rETH returns proxy: null and verified: true. Upgrades are performed by re-pointing a contract-name key to a new address in RocketStorage; RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade 0x9290AA076a2F1418a4E414E3D83AE03cA8E1ad10 emits ContractUpgraded(name, oldAddress, newAddress) and ContractAdded(name, newAddress). Registry indirection, not delegatecall proxies, is the upgrade mechanism.

oDAO upgrade path, stage by stage: (1) proposal raised on RocketDAONodeTrustedProposals 0xb0ec3F657ef43A615aB480FA8D5A53BF2c2f05d5; (2) voting cannot open for getVoteDelayTime() = 604800 s (7 days) read on RocketDAONodeTrustedSettingsProposals 0xAD038f8994a6bd51C8A72D3721CEd83401D4d2b0 at block 25883993, with getVoteTime() = 1209600 s and getExecuteTime() = 2419200 s; (3) execution calls RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade.upgrade(string,string,string,address), which (version() = 2) creates a pending upgrade — the contract exposes getEnd(uint256), getState(uint256), getVetoed(uint256), veto(uint256) and a separate execute(uint256), and emits UpgradePending / UpgradeVetoed; (4) execute(uint256) after that pending window. Uncontested fast path is therefore at least 604800 s (7 days) of on-chain-verified delay plus the pending-upgrade delay.

pDAO parameter/treasury path is materially slower: RocketDAOProtocolSettingsProposals 0xf6ad771dfB1cd10c66F688E251b5E5c21cbfDF81 (version 3) at block 25246510 returns getVoteDelayTime() = 604800 s, getVotePhase1Time() = 604800 s, getVotePhase2Time() = 604800 s and getExecuteTime() = 2419200 s — a 1,814,400 s (21-day) minimum from proposal to executable, with a 28-day execution window.

No Gnosis Safe sits on the inspected control paths. The T1 actor is an on-chain committee contract, not a multisig: RocketDAONodeTrusted reports getMemberCount() = 10, getMemberMinRequired() = 3 and getMemberQuorumVotesRequired() = 5100000000000000000 (51% in 1e18 fixed point) at block 25778186. Member identities could not be enumerated because the defipunkd read API rejected every argument-taking call in this run (getMemberAt(uint256) returned HTTP 400).

pDAO governance is on-chain and RPL-stake-weighted with an optimistic fraud-proof design. RocketDAOProtocolProposal 0x2D627A50Dc1C4EDa73E42858E8460b0eCF300b25 (version 2, getTotal() = 10 at block 25884008) exposes propose(string,bytes,uint32,tuple[]), vote(uint256,uint8,uint256,uint256,tuple[]) with a merkle witness, overrideVote(uint256,uint8) for delegators, destroy, finalise and execute. Constants from 0xf6ad771dfB1cd10c66F688E251b5E5c21cbfDF81: getProposalQuorum() = 150000000000000000 (15%), getProposalVetoQuorum() = 200000000000000000 (20%), getProposalBond() = 100000000000000000000 (100 RPL), getChallengeBond() = 10000000000000000000 (10 RPL), getChallengePeriod() = 1800 s, getProposalMaxBlockAge() = 1024 blocks.

A separate veto authority exists and is wired into the deployed upgrade contract: RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade v2 exposes veto(uint256) and getVetoed(uint256) and emits UpgradeVetoed. RPIP-60 (a protocol-owned domain) specifies that upgrades carry an upgrade_delay (initial value 1 week) during which a pDAO-elected security council may veto, with veto quorum parameter rocketDAOProtocolSettingsSecurity.upgradeveto.quorum initially 33%. The security council's own contract address, member count and threshold were not located on-chain this run.

Highest reachable tier is T1. The binding function is RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade.upgrade(string,string,string,address), which re-registers an arbitrary address under an arbitrary network contract name in RocketStorage. Because Rocket Pool's fund-holding and accounting contracts are resolved by name from RocketStorage at call time (rETH resolves rocketDepositPool and rocketNetworkBalances by name, and rETH.mint is gated only by onlyLatestContract("rocketDepositPool", msg.sender)), a successful upgrade can install a contract that mints rETH or moves protocol ETH. That is fund-critical, not merely governance-internal.

The pDAO path is T2 at most for parameters and treasury (RocketDAOProtocol exposes bootstrapSpendTreasury and bootstrapSetting* only under a now-disabled bootstrap flag; live treasury/parameter changes route through the 21-day RocketDAOProtocolProposal path). One pDAO-settable parameter reaches user liquidity indirectly: rETH._beforeTokenTransfer reads network.reth.deposit.delay from the dao.protocol.setting.network namespace and blocks transfer/burn until that many blocks have passed since the holder's last deposit; no on-chain upper bound on that setting was verified in this run.

steelman.red: A single permissioned 10-member committee, whose membership this run could not enumerate, can point any protocol contract name at arbitrary bytecode via upgrade(string,string,string,address), and the guardian EOA returned by getGuardian() is still a live address on the storage root.
steelman.orange: T1 is reachable, and although the on-chain-verified vote delay alone is 604800 s (7 days), the actor holding it is a closed 10-member committee that admits its own members and whose signer identities, insider status and public announcement could not be verified this run, so the Security Council standard cannot be certified and the second delay component (upgrade_delay) was not re-read on-chain.
steelman.green: Bootstrap mode is disabled on both DAO contracts, the uncontested oDAO fast path already carries 604800 s of on-chain-verified delay before voting can even open, a deployed veto(uint256) function plus UpgradeVetoed event give an independent body a hard stop on upgrades, and the pDAO parameter path is a 21-day RPL-weighted on-chain vote with a 15% quorum and bonded fraud-proof challenges.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the highest reachable tier is T1 via RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade.upgrade(string,string,string,address) — a function that re-registers any network contract name in RocketStorage 0x1d8f8f00cfa6758d7bE78336684788Fb0ee0Fa46 and thereby reaches rETH minting and protocol ETH — and the holder of that power is RocketDAONodeTrusted 0xb8e783882b11Ff4f6Cef3C501EA0f4b960152cc9 with getMemberCount() = 10 and a 51% quorum whose members I could not enumerate on-chain. The green steel-man is real: getVoteDelayTime() = 604800 s is verified on 0xAD038f8994a6bd51C8A72D3721CEd83401D4d2b0, the deployed upgrade contract is version 2 with veto(uint256)/getVetoed(uint256)/UpgradeVetoed, and both bootstrap flags read true (disabled). But the green branch of the rubric requires either a certified Security Council or broad token-distributed governance sitting on the T1 path, and neither is established here: signer identities, insider fraction and public announcement of the oDAO are unverified, the separate security council's address and threshold were not located, and the pending-upgrade delay was corroborated only from RPIP-60 prose rather than re-read on-chain. The red steel-man is weaker than orange because no single EOA or 2-of-3 multisig holds T1 — the guardian's bootstrap entrypoints are dead per two on-chain reads — and the T1 authority is an auditable smart contract with a non-zero, verified delay.

evidence.shows: RocketStorage: getDeployedStatus() = true and getGuardian() = 0x0cCF14983364A7735d369879603930Afe10df21e at block 25883993; write surface includes setAddress/setUint/setBool/setGuardian and the ABI is sourced from etherscan.

RocketDAONodeTrusted at block 25778186: getBootstrapModeDisabled() = true, getMemberCount() = 10, getMemberMinRequired() = 3, getMemberQuorumVotesRequired() = 5100000000000000000; write surface includes bootstrapUpgrade and bootstrapMember.

RocketDAONodeTrustedSettingsProposals at block 25883993: getVoteDelayTime() = 604800, getVoteTime() = 1209600, getExecuteTime() = 2419200, getCooldownTime() = 172800, getActionTime() = 2419200 — the oDAO proposal timing constants.

RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade version() = 2 with write functions upgrade(string,string,string,address), execute(uint256), veto(uint256), bootstrapUpgrade(...); view functions getEnd/getState/getVetoed/getUpgradeAddress; events UpgradePending, UpgradeVetoed, ContractUpgraded, ContractAdded — establishing a pending-then-execute upgrade flow with a veto stage.
Block-pinned read (blockNumber 25793884, blockHash 0xd39661fe...): getTotal() = 1 upgrade proposal recorded on the v2 upgrade contract, with raw calldata 0x775a25e3 and rawReturnData included.

RocketDAOProtocol at block 25793758: getBootstrapModeDisabled() = true; write surface is entirely bootstrapSetting*/bootstrapSpendTreasury/bootstrapDisable, i.e. guardian-only paths that the disabled flag closes.

RocketDAOProtocolSettingsProposals version 3 at block 25246510: getVoteDelayTime() = 604800, getVotePhase1Time() = 604800, getVotePhase2Time() = 604800, getExecuteTime() = 2419200, getProposalQuorum() = 150000000000000000, getProposalVetoQuorum() = 200000000000000000, getProposalBond() = 100000000000000000000, getChallengeBond() = 10000000000000000000, getChallengePeriod() = 1800.
RocketDAOProtocolProposal version() = 2, getTotal() = 10 at block 25884008; write surface propose/vote/overrideVote/destroy/finalise/execute with merkle-witness voting and delegate override.

rETH source at a pinned commit: mint() is gated only by onlyLatestContract("rocketDepositPool", msg.sender), and getEthValue/getTotalCollateral resolve rocketNetworkBalances and rocketDepositPool by name through RocketStorage — the basis (derived) for the claim that re-registering a name in RocketStorage reaches rETH issuance and protocol ETH. Also shows _beforeTokenTransfer enforcing the network.reth.deposit.delay setting.

Protocol-owned RPIP specifying upgrade_delay (initial value 1 week) between an upgrade passing and executing, and a security council veto over oDAO-proposed contract upgrades with rocketDAOProtocolSettingsSecurity.upgradeveto.quorum initially 33%. Corroboration only — these values were not re-read on-chain in this run.

Rocket Pool subdomain stating Saturn I launched to mainnet on 18 Feb 2026 with 'Protocol upgrade guardrails — a mandatory delay period will be enforced before protocol upgrades go live, during which the security council can veto changes', consistent with the deployed v2 upgrade contract's veto surface.

unknowns: C3: the pending-upgrade delay enforced between RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade.upgrade() and execute() could not be read on-chain — the contract exposes no zero-argument delay getter, and every argument-taking /api/contract/read call in this run (getEnd(1), getState(1), getName(1)) returned HTTP 400. Value taken from RPIP-60 prose (1 week initial) as corroboration only; not re-read on-chain this run.

C4: oDAO member addresses could not be enumerated. getMemberAt(uint256) requires an argument and the read API rejected all argument-bearing requests this run, so insider vs non-insider classification and public-announcement status of the 10 members are undetermined.

C4: no Gnosis Safe was found on any inspected path; /api/safe/owners was not exercised because no candidate Safe address was surfaced. Ops, incentives and grants multisigs, if any exist, were not located and their scope is undetermined.

C6: the security council contract address, member count, threshold and the live value of rocketDAOProtocolSettingsSecurity.upgradeveto.quorum were not located on-chain. The veto power is evidenced only by the deployed veto(uint256) function plus RPIP-60 prose.
C6: RPIP-33 emergency response settings changes referenced by RPIP-60 were not inspected; whether a fast emergency setting path with a different time cap exists on-chain is undetermined.

C1: the exact access modifier guarding RocketStorage.setAddress/setGuardian was not read from source this run (only the ABI was read), so the claim that only registered network contracts can write to storage is not independently verified here.

C5: pDAO voting-power source (staked-RPL snapshot weighting) and the current distribution of that voting power were not read on-chain; getVotingPowerRequired(uint256) takes an argument and could not be called.

RocketDAONodeTrusted — 10-member oDAO committee, 51% quorum, bootstrap disabled
RocketDAOProtocolProposal v2 — pDAO parameter/treasury proposal engine
RocketDAOProtocol — bootstrap entrypoints, bootstrap mode disabled

protocol_metadata.about: Users deposit ETH and receive rETH, a transferable receipt token whose ETH value grows as the protocol's validators earn consensus and execution rewards; holders redeem by calling burn() against whatever ETH collateral the protocol holds, or by selling rETH on secondary markets. The distinctive mechanism is permissionless node operation: independent operators post a partial bond (halved to 4 ETH under the Saturn I upgrade) and are matched with pooled staker ETH to run 32 ETH validators, rather than the operator set being curated by the DAO. Contracts are not proxies — every network contract is resolved by name through an immutable RocketStorage key-value registry, and upgrades work by re-registering a name to a new address.

headline: rETH burn() is fully permissionless with no pause guard or role check, but it is liquidity-gated and getTotalCollateral() read 1 wei at block 25793869, so primary redemption is currently unavailable in practice and a pDAO-set transfer delay parameter with no verified upper bound sits in front of every transfer and burn.
short_headline: Permissionless burn, but collateral reads zero

findings.text: The user-facing exit surface on rETH 0xae78736Cd615f374D3085123A210448E74Fc6393 is exactly one function: burn(uint256). The full non-view write surface is burn, mint, depositExcess and depositExcessCollateral; there is no requestWithdrawal, no claim, no exit, and no withdrawal queue on the token. Secondary transfer (transfer/transferFrom) is the only other way out.

burn(uint256) at pinned commit 967e4d3c is declared `external` with no access modifier, no onlyRole, no whenNotPaused and no _checkResumed. Its only requires are: amount > 0, caller balance sufficient, and getTotalCollateral() >= ethAmount ('Insufficient ETH balance for exchange'). mint() by contrast is gated by onlyLatestContract("rocketDepositPool", msg.sender). There is no separate request-placement versus claim-finalized split on rETH — burn is atomic.

A second gate applies to every transfer and burn: _beforeTokenTransfer reads network.reth.deposit.delay from the dao.protocol.setting.network namespace and reverts with 'Not enough time has passed since deposit' until that many blocks have elapsed since the caller's last deposit. This is a pDAO-settable parameter; no on-chain upper-bound check on it was verified in this run.

There is no queue, but redemption is collateral-gated and the collateral currently reads as effectively empty: at block 25793869 getTotalCollateral() = 1 (wei) and getCollateralRate() = 0, against a totalSupply() of 320132918084868744550713 rETH and getExchangeRate() = 1169905281654818538. Source at pinned commit confirms getTotalCollateral() = rocketDepositPool.getExcessBalance() + address(this).balance. On that read, burn() would revert for any non-trivial amount.

No frontend dependency for exit. rETH is verified on Etherscan (/api/contract/abi returns verified: true, abiSource etherscan, proxy: null) and burn(uint256) is a plain external function on a non-proxy ERC-20, so any wallet, block-explorer write tab, or script with the public ABI can call it.

No pause guard exists to hold a role against: the rETH ABI contains no paused(), no isPaused, no PAUSE_ROLE, no hasRole and no access-control surface at all. The only actor-controlled lever on the rETH exit path found in this run is the pDAO-set network.reth.deposit.delay parameter described under E2.

steelman.red: Redemption at the protocol is presently not functioning — getTotalCollateral() returned 1 wei against a 320,132 rETH supply — and every transfer and burn passes through a delay parameter set by governance for which no on-chain upper bound was verified, so a sufficiently large value would freeze holders out of both redemption and secondary sale.
steelman.orange: Exit is contractually permissionless and unpausable — burn() has no modifier, no role check and no pause guard, and there is no queue and no admin signature — but the primary redemption route is gated on deposit-pool excess liquidity that currently reads as zero, and a governance-settable per-holder transfer delay sits in front of it with no verified bound.
steelman.green: burn(uint256) is `external` with no access control whatsoever, callable directly from any wallet against a verified non-proxy ERC-20 with no frontend involved, no pause role exists anywhere in the contract, and there is no queue, no admin approval and no claim-versus-request split that could be gated differently.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because the contractual exit is genuinely permissionless — burn(uint256) at commit 967e4d3c carries no modifier, no role check and no pause guard, and /api/contract/abi confirms rETH is a verified non-proxy contract callable without any frontend — yet two things stop this from being green. First, the on-chain read at block 25793869 shows getTotalCollateral() = 1 wei and getCollateralRate() = 0 against a 320,132 rETH supply, so the burn path's own require would revert today; primary redemption is not an available exit at this snapshot even though nobody paused it. Second, _beforeTokenTransfer routes every transfer and burn through network.reth.deposit.delay, a pDAO-set parameter for which I did not verify an on-chain upper bound, which is a governance lever on exit even if a benign one at its current value. The red steel-man overstates the case: a liquidity shortfall is not a pause, no actor holds a pause role on this contract, secondary transfer remains available to anyone past the deposit delay, and nothing here lets any actor gate claims of already-finalized exits. The green steel-man understates it, because a redemption function that reverts for want of collateral is not an exit a user can actually take on their own terms.

evidence.shows: rETH pre-executed reads at block 25793869 (blockHash 0x199ce4d3...): getTotalCollateral() = 1, getCollateralRate() = 0, getExchangeRate() = 1169905281654818538, totalSupply() = 320132918084868744550713, version() = 1. Full write surface is burn(uint256), mint(uint256,address), depositExcess(), depositExcessCollateral() — no pause, no role, no queue functions.

verified: true, abiSource: etherscan, proxy: null, contractName RocketTokenRETH — the exit function's ABI is public and the contract is directly callable without the project's frontend, and there is no implementation contract behind it.

burn(uint256) declared external with no access modifier and only three requires (amount > 0, sufficient balance, getTotalCollateral() >= ethAmount); mint gated by onlyLatestContract('rocketDepositPool'); getTotalCollateral() = depositPool.getExcessBalance() + address(this).balance; _beforeTokenTransfer enforcing network.reth.deposit.delay on every non-mint transfer.

RocketDAOProtocolSettingsProposals: any pDAO change to a protocol setting such as network.reth.deposit.delay must pass getVoteDelayTime() 604800 + getVotePhase1Time() 604800 + getVotePhase2Time() 604800 = 21 days, establishing the time bound on the one governance lever identified on the exit path.

unknowns: E3: no pause guard exists on rETH itself, but RocketDepositPool's deposit.enabled / assign.enabled settings and any RocketDAOProtocolSettingsDeposit pause flags were not read this run — the deposit pool address was not in the pinned address_book and the allowlist rejects surfacer URLs for addresses not discovered from a defipunkd source, so whether an actor can halt the excess-balance path that feeds burn() is undetermined.
E3: no on-chain upper bound on the network.reth.deposit.delay setting was verified. RocketDAOProtocolSettingsNetwork was not inspected, so whether its setter enforces a maximum is undetermined.

E4: the emergency-versus-governance pause distinction could not be resolved. RPIP-60 references RPIP-33 emergency response settings taken directly by the security council, but that council's contract, its scope and any time cap were not located on-chain this run.

E5: no maximum queue duration or daily withdrawal cap exists on rETH, but why getTotalCollateral() reads 1 wei at block 25793869 was not investigated — whether this is a transient post-Saturn routing state or a sustained condition is undetermined.

E6: no forced-exit or permissionless escape hatch was found in the rETH ABI or source. Whether any protocol-level emergency exit exists elsewhere (e.g. a megapool-side user-distribute path) was not checked.

E1: node-operator-side exits were not enumerated. Saturn I introduced megapools with their own claim and capital-distribution functions; the megapool factory and delegate addresses were not in the pinned address_book and were not inspected, so operator-side exit gating is undetermined.

headline: No external oracle, bridge or third-party contract sits in the rETH path — the only non-substrate dependency is Rocket Pool's own 10-member oDAO committee reporting validator balances that set the rETH exchange rate; a Saturn balance-submission guardrail is documented but its on-chain activation was not verified, leaving impacted TVS at ~<1% for a single-member failure and up to ~100% of rETH TVS only under 6-of-10 collusion.
short_headline: oDAO committee sets rETH rate; guardrail unverified

findings.text: The rETH pricing path contains no external contract. At pinned commit 967e4d3c, getEthValue and getRethValue read getTotalETHBalance() and getTotalRETHSupply() from RocketNetworkBalances, and getTotalCollateral reads RocketDepositPool — both resolved by name from RocketStorage. There is no Chainlink, Pyth or Redstone feed, no latestAnswer/latestRoundData call, no AMM pool read and no external yield wrapper anywhere in the token's dependency graph. rETH itself is verified with proxy: null.

The dominant non-substrate dependency is Rocket Pool's own oracle committee. RocketDAONodeTrusted 0xb8e783882b11Ff4f6Cef3C501EA0f4b960152cc9 reads getMemberCount() = 10, getMemberMinRequired() = 3 and getMemberQuorumVotesRequired() = 5100000000000000000 (51%) at block 25778186. Members are admitted through the oDAO's own proposal process (memberJoinRequired, bootstrapMember). This committee reports validator balances and the RPL:ETH ratio into the protocol; because rETH's getEthValue derives directly from the reported total ETH balance, a coordinated mis-report by a 6-of-10 majority moves the rate at which rETH mints and burns.

Node-operator and validator risk is NOT counted here. Rocket Pool's operator set is permissionless and large — the protocol's design is that independent operators post a partial bond and are matched with pooled ETH — which places it on the diversified/bonded mitigated path rather than the small-operator-set path. Validator slashing is Ethereum PoS substrate, not a Rocket Pool dependency.

The collateral chain is depth 1. rETH is backed by ETH staked directly in Ethereum validators; there is no LST, LRT, ERC-4626 wrapper or restaking layer beneath it. No actor other than the base-chain protocol and the validator's own withdrawal credentials holds slashing or freezing power at any level below rETH.

Fallback status, stated explicitly per A6: (i) LIVE and enforcing — the 51% consensus threshold on oDAO submissions, evidenced on-chain by getMemberQuorumVotesRequired() = 5100000000000000000, means no single reporter can move the rate. (iii) DOCUMENTED only — the Saturn 'balance submission guardrail' constraining oDAO-submitted balance data is described on the protocol's Saturn site as shipped with the 18 Feb 2026 mainnet launch, but I could not read its bound values or confirm its activation on-chain in this run, so per the A6 rule it does not reduce the risk in the steel-man or verdict. (i) LIVE — the burn-side require getTotalCollateral() >= ethAmount caps ETH extraction at collateral actually held regardless of what rate is reported.

Not applicable. Rocket Pool is deployed on Ethereum mainnet and is not its own L2, L3 or appchain; there is no protocol-owned sequencer or DA layer. Ethereum consensus and the canonical deposit contract are substrate, not dependencies.

oDAO watchtower daemons are a necessary-but-permissioned off-chain actor. If they stop submitting, the rETH exchange rate goes stale and rewards-tree generation halts; the degradation is graceful — rETH keeps trading, burn keeps working against existing collateral, and nothing becomes insolvent — rather than catastrophic. There is no liquidation-bot or keeper-solvency dependency in this design because there are no leveraged positions to liquidate.

The governance-mutable external-dependency surface is narrow because the trusted reporter set IS the dependency: changing who reports balances means changing oDAO membership, which routes through the oDAO's own proposal path with getVoteDelayTime() = 604800 s (7 days) plus a 1209600 s vote window on 0xAD038f8994a6bd51C8A72D3721CEd83401D4d2b0. No oracle address swap is possible because no external oracle address is referenced. Re-registering rocketNetworkBalances to a different contract is an upgrade action and is covered under the control slice, not A9.

steelman.red: A 6-of-10 permissioned committee determines the total-ETH-balance figure from which rETH's exchange rate is computed, the guardrail that is supposed to bound their submissions is documented but was not verified as live on-chain in this run, and a deflated report would let an attacker mint rETH cheaply and dilute every existing holder's principal.
steelman.orange: The only non-substrate dependency is an internal 10-member committee whose submissions require 51% agreement (verified on-chain) and whose worst realistic single-member failure is a stale rate rather than a loss, while the burn-side collateral require caps ETH extraction at collateral actually held — so ordinary failures degrade performance and freshness rather than principal, and principal loss requires a majority-collusion tail event.
steelman.green: There is not a single external contract in the rETH path — no oracle feed, no bridge, no AMM, no nested receipt token, no keeper — and the collateral chain is depth 1 straight to Ethereum validators, so no third party's failure can touch this protocol at all.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange. Module weighting: rETH liquid staking is ~100% of user-facing TVS (grade: orange) and is the only module holding staker principal; the operator-side minipool and Saturn megapool modules hold node-operator bond capital rather than staker deposits and their split could not be quantified (flagged in unknowns), so the weighted overall is set by the rETH module at orange. The green steel-man is genuinely strong on A1 and A4 — I found no external contract call anywhere in the rETH path, no oracle feed address, no bridge and a depth-1 collateral chain — but it fails on A2: the total-ETH-balance figure feeding getEthValue comes from a 10-member permissioned committee (getMemberCount() = 10, 51% quorum verified at block 25778186), which is exactly the off-chain-committee-reporting-in case this slice counts. The red steel-man is the closer call and I rank orange above it for three concrete reasons: the 51% threshold is verified live on-chain so no single reporter can act; the burn path's own require (getTotalCollateral() >= ethAmount at commit 967e4d3c) caps ETH extraction at collateral actually held, which at block 25793869 read 1 wei; and the ETH itself sits in beacon-chain validators whose withdrawal credentials the committee does not control. Impacted TVS: ~<1% for any single-member failure or a stale-rate outage; up to ~100% of rETH TVS only in the 6-of-10 collusion tail, and I am not counting the Saturn balance guardrail as mitigation because I could not verify it is enforcing on-chain.

evidence.shows: Full rETH source at a pinned commit: the only external reads are RocketNetworkBalances.getTotalETHBalance/getTotalRETHSupply and RocketDepositPool.getExcessBalance/withdrawExcessBalance, both resolved by name via getContractAddress through RocketStorage. No Chainlink/Pyth/Redstone import, no latestAnswer, no getPrice, no AMM or vault call. Also shows the burn-side collateral require that caps extraction.

The oracle committee's live size and threshold at block 25778186: getMemberCount() = 10, getMemberMinRequired() = 3, getMemberQuorumVotesRequired() = 5100000000000000000 (51%), getBootstrapModeDisabled() = true; membership is admitted via memberJoinRequired / bootstrapMember on this contract.

Live rETH state at block 25793869 showing the reported-rate output and the collateral cap that bounds it: getExchangeRate() = 1169905281654818538, getTotalCollateral() = 1, getCollateralRate() = 0, totalSupply() = 320132918084868744550713.

verified: true, proxy: null, 21 functions — the deployed rETH ABI contains no oracle-consumer method (no latestAnswer, latestRoundData, getPrice or aggregator setter), corroborating on the deployed bytecode's interface that no external feed is wired in.
The time bound on changing the trusted reporter set: oDAO proposals carry getVoteDelayTime() = 604800 s and getVoteTime() = 1209600 s at block 25883993.

Protocol subdomain stating Saturn I went live on Ethereum mainnet 18 Feb 2026 and listing 'Balance submission guardrail — Saturn introduces constraints on oDAO-submitted balance data, protecting the rETH protocol rate from manipulation or faulty reporting'. Recorded as DOCUMENTED-only per A6; activation not verified on-chain.

RocketDAOProtocolProposal version() = 2 and RocketDAOProtocolSettingsProposals version 3 elsewhere in this run corroborate that Saturn-era contract versions are deployed on mainnet, supporting the claim that the Saturn upgrade set is live even though the specific guardrail bounds were not read.

unknowns: A6: the Saturn balance-submission guardrail's on-chain activation status and bound values could not be determined. headline: No contract-level whitelist, KYC or blocklist on rETH entry or exit and no operator approval in the admission path; the contract is verified, non-proxy and its ABI is public, and the full source is open on GitHub, so admission does not depend on the official publisher's cooperation.

findings.text: No whitelist or role gate on user entry or exit. The rETH source at pinned commit 967e4d3c contains no onlyWhitelisted, no onlyRole, no allowlist, no isAccredited and no isKYCed; the deployed ABI contains no hasRole, getRoleAdmin, grantRole or any access-control surface. burn(uint256) is declared `external` with no modifier at all. The single onlyLatestContract modifier on the contract sits on mint() and depositExcess() and gates which protocol contract may call them — it is internal routing, not a gate on which humans may enter.

There is no contract-level sanctions or compliance check. The rETH ABI and source contain no OFAC list read, no on-chain blocklist mapping, no screening-oracle call and no blacklist/unblacklist admin function. Nothing in the contract can mark an address as ineligible to hold, transfer or redeem rETH.

Read access and write access are both permissionless. Every rETH view method executes for any caller — the surfacer pre-executed decimals, getCollateralRate, getExchangeRate, getTotalCollateral, name, symbol, totalSupply and version against public RPC endpoints at block 25793869 — and the write side (burn, transfer, transferFrom, approve) carries no caller restriction.

An independent access path exists and does not require the publisher. rETH is verified on Etherscan with proxy: null and a public 21-function ABI returned by /api/contract/abi, so any wallet, script, explorer write tab or third-party client can construct a burn(uint256) or transfer call without touching stake.rocketpool.net. The full protocol source is public on github.com/rocket-pool/rocketpool, fetched at commit 967e4d3c, and the Immunefi program page for Rocket Pool links github.com/rocket-pool as the project's code home.

No off-chain operator sits in the admission path for the rETH exit. burn(uint256) admits any holder unconditionally subject only to their own balance and available collateral — no keeper signature, no relayer, no oracle poster approval and no sequencer. The oDAO's balance submissions affect the rate at which a redemption settles, not whether the caller is admitted to make it; that liveness dependency is graded in the autonomy slice.

Frontend posture recorded as context only, not as a grade lever: the official site rocketpool.net returns a JavaScript-only shell ('We're sorry but the Rocket Pool website doesn't work properly without JavaScript enabled') and docs.rocketpool.net serves an identical SPA shell for every path, so neither A3-passive ToS clauses nor any A3-active runtime enforcement (geo-block, wallet screening, jurisdiction banner) could be observed. No A3-active enforcement is asserted in either direction.

steelman.red: The official interface's terms of service and any runtime geo-blocking or wallet-screening could not be read because both rocketpool.net and docs.rocketpool.net render only a JavaScript shell, so an active jurisdictional gate on the publisher's client cannot be ruled out.
steelman.orange: The independent access paths I can name are the generic ones available for any verified ERC-20 — direct contract calls and the open-source repo — rather than an enumerated third-party frontend, wallet integration or aggregator route confirmed by a fetched page.
steelman.green: The contracts carry no whitelist, no KYC check, no on-chain blocklist and no operator approval anywhere in the entry or exit path, and rETH is a verified non-proxy ERC-20 with a public ABI and fully open source, so anyone can enter and exit through any client they choose.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because the grade on this slice turns on what the contract permits and whether the protocol is reachable without the publisher, and both answers are clean. The rETH source at commit 967e4d3c has no whitelist modifier, no role check and no compliance hook on any user-facing function, and the deployed ABI returned by /api/contract/abi confirms the same 21-function surface with no access-control methods and no blocklist. burn(uint256) admits any holder with a balance; no keeper, relayer or oracle poster must approve the action for it to be accepted. The independent path test is satisfied by the contract being verified, non-proxy and ABI-public — any wallet or script can call it — plus the full source being open at github.com/rocket-pool/rocketpool. The red steel-man is a documentation gap, not a finding: I could not read the ToS because the site is a JS shell, and per this slice's rules frontend ToS and A3-active enforcement are publisher policies reported as context and cannot move the grade when contracts are permissionless. The orange steel-man would require me to affirmatively show that all independent paths are absent or gated, and the opposite is demonstrated — the ABI is public and the code is open.

evidence.shows: Complete rETH source: burn(uint256) declared external with no modifier; the only modifier used anywhere is onlyLatestContract('rocketDepositPool', msg.sender) on mint and depositExcess; no onlyWhitelisted, onlyRole, allowlist, KYC or sanctions check appears in the file.

verified: true, abiSource: etherscan, proxy: null, counts 21 functions and 5 events, with the full ABI inlined — the exit function's calling convention is public, so any client can reach the contract without the official frontend. No hasRole/grantRole/blacklist entries appear in the ABI.

All eight zero-argument view methods pre-executed successfully against public RPC at block 25793869, demonstrating read-permissionless state; the listed write surface is burn/mint/depositExcess/depositExcessCollateral with no admission-gating function.

Rocket Pool's public program page linking github.com/rocket-pool as the project's code home and describing the protocol as decentralised and non-custodial; also records that KYC is required for bug-bounty payout processing, which is a researcher-payout condition and not a condition on protocol usage.

The official site returns a JavaScript-only shell ('We're sorry but the Rocket Pool website doesn't work properly without JavaScript enabled'), which is why no ToS clause or runtime jurisdiction banner could be extracted; recorded as the reason for the A6 unknown.
The documentation site serves an identical Rspress SPA shell for every path rather than page content, confirming the extraction failure is site-wide and not path-specific.

unknowns: A6: no verbatim ToS or eligibility clause could be extracted. rocketpool.net returns a JS-only shell and docs.rocketpool.net returns the same SPA shell for every path; no ToS URL rendered content this run. Per the slice rules the clause text is not paraphrased or inferred and no assertion is made about its content.

A3: whether the official interface at stake.rocketpool.net applies A3-active enforcement (IP geo-blocking, wallet screening against a sanctions oracle, or a jurisdiction banner) could not be determined for the same SPA-render reason. No A3-active finding is claimed in either direction.

A3b: no specific third-party frontend, wallet integration or aggregator route was confirmed by a fetched page this run. The independent-path finding rests on the verified public ABI and open-source repo rather than on an enumerated alternative UI.

A2: the deposit-side admission path was not inspected. RocketDepositPool was not in the pinned address_book and could not be surfaced, so whether the deposit entry point carries any gate (e.g. a deposits-enabled flag or a per-address restriction) distinct from the exit path is undetermined.
A1: node-operator registration and Saturn megapool entry were not inspected; whether operator-side admission (as distinct from rETH staker admission) carries any allowlist is undetermined.

headline: Every governance and token contract inspected resolves a verified ABI from Etherscan or Sourcify with no proxies to chase, the explorer-visible rETH source matches the public repo at a pinned commit, and three audits — Cantina, Bailsec and Sigma Prime — landed within eight weeks of the Saturn I mainnet launch.

findings.text: Seven of the eight pinned governance and token addresses resolve a verified ABI. Sourced from etherscan: RocketStorage 0x1d8f8f00cfa6758d7bE78336684788Fb0ee0Fa46, RocketDAONodeTrusted 0xb8e783882b11Ff4f6Cef3C501EA0f4b960152cc9, RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade 0x9290AA076a2F1418a4E414E3D83AE03cA8E1ad10, RocketDAONodeTrustedSettingsProposals 0xAD038f8994a6bd51C8A72D3721CEd83401D4d2b0, RocketDAOProtocol 0x0429Cdd8cEACe24d4dC2B97Ce22A780a407dF0e1, RocketDAOProtocolProposal 0x2D627A50Dc1C4EDa73E42858E8460b0eCF300b25, RocketTokenRETH 0xae78736Cd615f374D3085123A210448E74Fc6393. Sourced from sourcify: RocketDAOProtocolSettingsProposals 0xf6ad771dfB1cd10c66F688E251b5E5c21cbfDF81. Each surfacer page names the resolved contract, which only happens when a verified source is found.

One pinned address fails verification: 0xCaC25e88276A333cF9d4196d112D93af67ef809A returns 'No verified ABI found ... (etherscan + sourcify both failed)' and the surfacer falls back to a generic probe battery. It is pinned as 'RocketDAOProtocol — pDAO core', but a verified contract named RocketDAOProtocol already resolves at 0x0429Cdd8cEACe24d4dC2B97Ce22A780a407dF0e1, so this looks like a stale or mis-classified address_book entry rather than a live core contract. Its actual role was not established this run.

There is nothing to chase behind a proxy. /api/contract/abi for rETH returns proxy: null, and none of the surfacer pages reported a proxy.implementation address. Rocket Pool upgrades by re-registering a contract name in RocketStorage rather than by delegatecall, so proxy-versus-implementation verification asymmetry does not arise: each registered address is itself directly verified.

Source-to-repo correspondence holds for the contract examined in depth. The explorer-derived rETH ABI (21 functions: burn, mint, depositExcess, depositExcessCollateral, getEthValue, getRethValue, getExchangeRate, getTotalCollateral, getCollateralRate plus ERC-20 surface, 5 events including TokensMinted/TokensBurned/EtherDeposited) matches function-for-function and event-for-event the source file at rocket-pool/rocketpool commit 967e4d3c32721a84694921751920af313d1467af. This is a structural correspondence, derived from comparing the two artifacts; no bytecode diff or local compile was performed.

Audit coverage is current relative to the deployment. The Rocket Pool Immunefi program lists, for the Saturn 1 release: Cantina completed 22 December 2025, Bailsec completed 29 January 2026, and Sigma Prime completed 5 February 2026. The Saturn I mainnet launch date is 18 February 2026 per the protocol's Saturn site, so the most recent in-scope review predates deployment by under two weeks and is roughly seven months old at analysis_date — well inside the 6-month-drift concern for a deployment that shipped after the audits. Earlier coverage includes Trail of Bits (30 April 2021), ConsenSys Diligence (30 April 2021, 31 May 2022, 31 December 2022, 30 November 2023 for Houston), Sigma Prime (2021, 2022, Houston 2024 and a Houston hotfix review 31 August 2024) and ChainSafe (31 March 2024).

The auditors are recognized. Sigma Prime, Trail of Bits and ConsenSys Diligence all appear on the recognized-firm list, and Sigma Prime — the firm that reviewed Saturn 1 most recently, on 5 February 2026 — is a Solidity-recognized firm with a multi-year engagement history on this codebase across the 2021, Redstone, Atlas, Houston and Saturn releases. Cantina and Bailsec are additional Saturn 1 reviewers; the green claim does not rest on them.

The bug bounty is live and current: maximum $150,000 for critical smart-contract findings with a $15,000 minimum, running since 8 September 2021, last updated 20 August 2026, with 77 assets in scope and a runnable PoC required.

steelman.red: One address in the pinned address_book, 0xCaC25e88276A333cF9d4196d112D93af67ef809A, has no verified source on either Etherscan or Sourcify, and if it turned out to be a live pDAO core contract that would be an unverified contract on a governance path.
steelman.orange: I pinned a repo commit for exactly one contract and never ran a bytecode diff or a compile-match for any of them, and the four oldest audits are five years stale relative to a codebase that has been through Redstone, Atlas, Houston, Saturn 0 and Saturn I since.
steelman.green: Every governance and token contract actually inspected resolves a verified ABI with no proxy indirection to obscure it, the deployed rETH interface corresponds function-for-function to the public repo at a pinned commit, and three separate firms including Sigma Prime audited Saturn 1 in the eight weeks before its 18 February 2026 mainnet launch.

rationale.verdict: Choosing green because all three green conditions hold on the contracts that matter. Verification: seven of eight pinned governance and token addresses resolve verified sources (six via Etherscan, one via Sourcify), and /api/contract/abi confirms rETH is verified with proxy: null, so there is no proxy-with-unverified-implementation gap anywhere — Rocket Pool's registry-indirection upgrade model means each registered address is itself directly verified. Repo correspondence: the deployed rETH ABI's 21 functions and 5 events match the source file at rocket-pool/rocketpool commit 967e4d3c function-for-function. Audit freshness: Cantina (2025-12-22), Bailsec (2026-01-29) and Sigma Prime (2026-02-05) reviewed Saturn 1 before its 2026-02-18 mainnet launch, and Sigma Prime is a recognized firm with continuous engagement across this codebase's release history. The red steel-man rests on 0xCaC25e88276A333cF9d4196d112D93af67ef809A having no verified source, but a verified RocketDAOProtocol already resolves at 0x0429Cdd8cEACe24d4dC2B97Ce22A780a407dF0e1 with the expected bootstrap surface, so the unverified entry reads as address_book noise rather than a live core contract — I flag it prominently in unknowns rather than let an unresolved label drive a red. The orange steel-man reduces to two scope limits of mine, not properties of the protocol: I did not run a bytecode diff and I did not sample the post-audit diff, both of which the rubric explicitly says belong in unknowns rather than in a downgrade.

evidence.shows: verified: true, abiSource: 'etherscan', contractName 'RocketTokenRETH', proxy: null, counts {functions: 21, events: 5}, warnings empty — the explicit verification indicator plus confirmation there is no implementation contract to verify separately.

173-line source file at a pinned commit whose function and event set (burn, mint, depositExcess, depositExcessCollateral, getEthValue, getRethValue, getExchangeRate, getTotalCollateral, getCollateralRate, EtherDeposited, TokensMinted, TokensBurned) corresponds to the explorer-derived ABI — the basis for the derived source-to-repo correspondence claim.

'No verified ABI found for 0xCaC25e88276A333cF9d4196d112D93af67ef809A on chainId 1 (etherscan + sourcify both failed)' with a generic fallback probe list instead of a resolved contract name — the single verification gap among the pinned addresses.

Resolves as contract name 'RocketDAOProtocol' with ABI source 'etherscan' and a coherent bootstrapSetting*/bootstrapSpendTreasury/bootstrapDisable surface — the verified contract bearing the role the unverified 0xCaC25e88 address was pinned with.
Resolves as 'RocketStorage', ABI source 'etherscan', with a full 35-entry ABI rendered — verification confirmed for the registry that roots all address resolution.
Resolves as 'RocketDAONodeTrustedUpgrade', ABI source 'etherscan', version 2 — verification confirmed for the contract holding the upgrade authority.

Resolves as 'RocketDAOProtocolSettingsProposals' with ABI source 'sourcify' — verified via the alternative verification registry rather than Etherscan, which still satisfies independent source availability.

Full audit table with firm names and completion dates: Cantina 22 December 2025, Bailsec 29 January 2026, Sigma Prime 5 February 2026 for Saturn 1; plus Trail of Bits 30 April 2021, ConsenSys Diligence 2021/2022/2023, Sigma Prime 2021/2022/2024, ChainSafe 31 March 2024. Also bounty maximum $150,000, live since 8 September 2021, last updated 20 August 2026, 77 assets in scope.
Saturn I mainnet launch date of 18 February 2026, establishing that the three most recent audits (Dec 2025 – Feb 2026) predate rather than lag the currently-deployed release.

unknowns: V2: no bytecode diff or local compile-match was performed for any contract, and a deploy-commit SHA was pinned for only one contract (rETH, via a GitHub blob URL returned by search). The repo correspondence claimed is structural — ABI function/event set versus source file — not a proven bytecode equivalence. Recorded as a scope limit per the V2 rule, not as a downgrade.

V5: post-audit drift was not sampled. No drift finding is asserted in either direction.

V3: the specific contracts and commits in scope for each audit could not be recorded because the PDFs were not opened — only the firm names and completion dates from the Immunefi program table are cited.

V1: 0xCaC25e88276A333cF9d4196d112D93af67ef809A has no verified source and its actual on-chain role is undetermined. I could not confirm whether it holds code at all, whether it is a live pDAO contract, or whether the address_book label is simply stale. This address should be re-resolved in a future run before it is treated as either a core contract or as noise.

protocol_metadata.about: Users deposit ETH and receive rETH, a transferable receipt token that appreciates against ETH as the protocol's validators earn staking rewards, and redeem by calling burn() against protocol-held collateral. Node operation is permissionless: independent operators post a partial ETH bond and are matched with pooled staker deposits to run 32 ETH validators. Contracts are not proxies — every network contract is registered by name in an immutable RocketStorage registry and upgraded by re-registering that name.
